notes: D-01: the file part always sends Content-Type: application/octet-stream; the engine judges the real type from the bytes (http.DetectContentType), so no SDK duplicates a per-extension table.
D-02: the filename is raw UTF-8 inside a quoted filename="…"; only the double quote, CR and LF are escaped, as %22, %0D and %0A, and there is no filename* form.
Go builds the file part header with mime/multipart CreatePart; CreateFormFile backslash-escapes the filename and forces its own content type, and the stub parser rejects that form.
D-03: the body part is compact canonical JSON with key order query|prompt first then params, raw UTF-8 and no HTML escaping; params is omitted entirely when mode is unset.
Python uses json.dumps(…, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":")); Go uses an Encoder with SetEscapeHTML(false) and trims the trailing newline Encode appends; Java writes UTF-8 explicitly.
Golden inputs exclude U+2028 and U+2029 (Go escapes them even with HTML escaping off) and all C0 control characters (no JDK was available to verify Jackson's handling).
A filename containing " is a wire-bytes test only: the stub decodes %22 but the engine may read it literally (Pitfall 14), so never put stub knobs or engine assertions on such a name.
